summary: Cache-side memory throughput and load stalls limit the matmul, rather than DRAM bandwidth or compute.
reasoning: Memory SOL is 70.14% versus 38.53% compute throughput. L2 throughput reaches 74.96% with a 95.79% hit rate, while DRAM throughput is only 15.24%, locating pressure primarily in the cache-backed load path.

root_causes.cause: Partial utilization of global-load sectors increases memory traffic per useful operand byte.

evidence.interpretation: Global loads use only half of the bytes in each sector on average.
Substantial L2 throughput makes inefficient transactions a likely contributor to memory pressure.

fixes.fix: Tune operand load layouts and tile dimensions so adjacent lanes access adjacent elements along each operand's stride-1 dimension.
fixes.rationale: Improved coalescing and sector utilization can reduce cache traffic for the same useful operand data.

root_causes.cause: Operand-load latency is insufficiently hidden across K-loop iterations.

evidence.interpretation: Warps spend a large fraction of active cycles waiting on dependencies from L1TEX-path operations.
Moderate achieved occupancy limits the pool of warps available to hide load latency.

fixes.fix: Autotune Triton's num_stages for the K loop, benchmarking additional software-pipeline stages while monitoring shared-memory usage and occupancy.
fixes.rationale: Overlapping future operand loads with current dot products can reduce exposed load waits, provided additional buffering does not excessively reduce occupancy.
